text:
Travis Sanheim is the Flyers' top defenseman, and the job right now is mostly survival. He plays 25 minutes a night against the other team's best on a club that takes only 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, and with him on the ice that number improves by about four points. On this roster, that's a real contribution.

His scoring is right where it should be: nine points in 22 games, three goals on 3.9 expected, and two goals in his last three games, including a power move to the net to tie Wednesday's game in Edmonton that Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports called assertive. No luck either way on his on-ice numbers.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.3 wins last season, 23rd among 215 defensemen, with opponents getting fewer chances when he played and his competition in the 92nd percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had a third of his shots coming off the rush, almost double a typical defenseman. The only knock this month came from his coach's choices, not his play: O'Connor noted Rick Tocchet sending him out for a late power play as a safety-first move.
